problems.prompt: Build an event-driven RateLimiter class implementing a sliding window algorithm. It extends EventEmitter and tracks request timestamps per key. consume(key) allows up to maxRequests within windowMs and returns { allowed, remaining, resetMs }. When a request exceeds the limit, it emits a 'blocked' event with (key, resetMs) and returns allowed: false. reset(key) clears the history for the specified key.

should emit 'blocked' event on rate limit breach
should slide window over time and restore allowance

hiddenTests.name: should track separate keys independently
should reset quota when reset(key) is invoked

steps.explain: Discard expired timestamps older than the sliding window interval to reclaim quota and memory.
Trigger real-time telemetry events allowing consumers to log or trigger blacklists.

should group array items by custom function iteratee

should omit items where property evaluates to undefined

problems.prompt: Implement a production-grade debounce(fn, delay) utility. It delays executing 'fn' until 'delay' milliseconds have elapsed since the last call. All subsequent calls within the delay window must reset the timer. The debounced function must preserve the invocation 'this' context and arguments.

visibleTests.name: should not execute synchronously and only fire once after 50ms
should reset the timer on each subsequent call within delay window

hiddenTests.name: should preserve execution 'this' context and multiple arguments
should support 0ms delay as a macrotask deferral

problems.checkpointHint: Store timer in closure scope and invoke clearTimeout(timer) before scheduling setTimeout.

steps.explain: Declare a local 'timer' variable in the outer closure so that each invocation of the returned wrapper function shares and mutates the same timer handle.
Cancel any pending scheduled task before queuing a new timeout. When the timeout triggers, call 'fn.apply(this, args)' to preserve context.
